option.log: read a backup instead of the log in your storage
option.json: print JSON, for agents and scripts

log.none: There is no log to read. Choose your storage with ./touchdown storage, or give a backup with --log FILE.

where.invalid: --where takes DIM=VALUE, or several values of one dimension: DIM=A,B (not "{item}").
where.twice: {id} is given twice: give its values together, {id}=A,B.
where.noValueSome: No {dimension} "{value}" among the log's {dataset}. Some there are: {some}.
flights.help: Your flights, newest first, as the Flights page lists them.
flights.option.airline: flown with this airline: its IATA or ICAO code, or its name
flights.option.airport: from or to this airport: its IATA or ICAO code
flights.option.type: on this type: its ICAO type code (A21N)
flights.option.search:
as the Flights page's search: flight number, airports, cities, registration, airline, type,
or a route: "SHA-PEK" either way, "SHA > PEK" one way
flights.option.recorded: only flights with a recorded track
flights.summary: {count, plural, one {# flight} other {# flights}} in {year, select, all {all years} other {{year}}}.
flights.summaryDistance: {count, plural, one {# flight} other {# flights}} in {year, select, all {all years} other {{year}}}, {distance}.
flight.help:
One flight, as its page in the web app shows it: every field, the aircraft, the track and the open findings.
Ticket numbers and booking references are never shown, only whether one is recorded.
flight.option.ref: the flight's id, or its flight number and day: XY123@2025-04-02
flight.exit: Exit status: 0 shown, 1 no such flight (or several: their ids are listed), 2 the log could not be read.
sightings.help: The aircraft you photographed, newest first.
sightings.option.airport: at this airport: its IATA or ICAO code
sightings.option.airline: of this airline: its IATA or ICAO code, or its name
sightings.option.type: of this type: its ICAO type code (B738)
sightings.summary: {count, plural, one {# sighting} other {# sightings}} of {aircraft, plural, one {# aircraft} other {# aircraft}} at {airports, plural, one {# airport} other {# airports}} in {year, select, all {all years} other {{year}}}.
sessions.help:
Your days out spotting, newest first: the day, the airport, how many sightings and aircraft, and how many of
those aircraft were new to your log.
sessions.summary: {count, plural, one {# day out} other {# days out}} in {year, select, all {all years} other {{year}}}.
aircraft.help:
Without REF, the aircraft in your log, as the Aircraft page lists them (last seen first). With REF, one
aircraft: what it is, its registrations and its timeline of flights and sightings.
aircraft.option.ref: the aircraft's id, or a registration (G-ABCD), on a date when it was reused (G-ABCD@2019-05-01)
aircraft.option.both: only aircraft you flew on and photographed
aircraft.option.provisional: only aircraft matched by registration until a serial number is known
aircraft.option.noFirstFlight: only aircraft without a first flight date
aircraft.option.search: registration, type, airline or serial number
aircraft.option.sort: last (the default), count (most records first) or reg
aircraft.summary: Your log holds {count, plural, one {# aircraft} other {# aircraft}}: you flew on {flown}, and {both} of those you also photographed.
aircraft.identity.provisional: matched by registration and date until the serial number is known
aircraft.timeline.title: Timeline: {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}
airport.help:
One airport, as its page in the web app shows it: how often you left from it, landed at it and changed planes
there, its flights, and the aircraft you photographed there.
airport.option.code: the airport's IATA or ICAO code
airport.exit: Exit status: 0 shown, 1 not an airport or not in your log, 2 the log could not be read.
airport.visits: {period, select, all {You} current {So far in {year} you} other {In {year} you}} {visits}.
airport.visits.changed: changed planes at {airport} {count, plural, =1 {once} =2 {twice} other {# times}}
airport.visits.changedThere: changed planes there {count, plural, =1 {once} =2 {twice} other {# times}}
airport.photographed: You photographed {aircraft, plural, one {# aircraft} other {# aircraft}} there on {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
airport.mostOften: Most often to or from {airport}: {count, plural, one {# flight} other {# flights}}.
airport.nothing: Nothing logged at {airport} in {year, select, all {all years} other {{year}}}.
issues.help:
The Issues page: fields changed on two devices before either saw the other's change (choose which to keep on the
Issues page in the web app), then every open finding, grouped by rule in the page's order, with the records it is
about and its suggested fixes. Each finding's id is the one to name it by. With --accepted, the warnings you marked
as right.
issues.option.severity: error, warning, info (notes), comma-separated, or all; errors and warnings by default
issues.option.rule: one rule only, such as C-FLIGHT-OVERLAP
issues.severityInvalid: --severity takes error, warning, info (comma-separated) or all.
issues.head: {parts}.
issues.head.conflicts: {count, plural, one {# field was} other {# fields were}} changed on two devices
issues.head.errors: {count, plural, one {# entry looks} other {# entries look}} wrong
issues.head.warnings: {count, plural, one {# entry is} other {# entries are}} worth a look
issues.head.nothing: Nothing to review. Every check passed or was accepted.
issues.notes: {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} besides (--severity info).
issues.conflict.deleted: Deleted on one device and changed on another; the entry was kept
issues.conflict.field: {field}: {kept} in your log, {other} from the other change
issues.conflict.choose: Choose which to keep on the Issues page in the web app.
issues.conflict.title: Changed on two devices <dim>· {count, plural, one {# field} other {# fields}}</dim>
issues.accepted.count: {count, plural, one {# accepted warning} other {# accepted warnings}}.
issues.accepted.gone: {title}<dim> (the values have changed since; it no longer applies)</dim>
imports.help:
The imports into your log, newest first, as the Import page's history lists them: when, the file, how many
rows were imported, and whether the import was undone. Each one's id is the one to undo it by.
stats.help:
Without --by: the Home page's sentence and facts for the period, then the Statistics page's figures and ranked
lists: flights, spotting and both (or only the part named). With --by: a table as in the Statistics page's
Custom view, one row per value of DIM (and one column per value of --cols).
stats.option.top: rows per ranked list (8, as on the page), or all
stats.option.cols: the columns, from the same list
stats.option.of:
flights (the default) or sightings; airport and phase are for sightings, from, to, route,
cabin and seatPosition for flights
stats.option.measure: records (the default), aircraft, distance or time (distance and time for flights)
stats.option.where:
only the records whose DIM is V, or one of V,W,…; repeat it for another dimension (all must hold).
A value as stored, as the page shows it, or a code: --where airline=BA,LH --where month=March
stats.option.view: a view saved on the Statistics page's Custom tab, or with stats views save, with its filters
stats.help.views:
stats views lists the saved views; save and remove change them as the other changing commands do: through the
inbox, for review (./touchdown help views).
